Play outer AI echoes the player without producing a situation or durable truths

In Shardwake play conversation play-conversation.f6da6961cc3f46b9ba6e6a9e171e5736, the player supplied an in-character return and direct speech to Mara. The assistant merely restated that text. currentSituation remained null and knownTruthCount remained zero.

The play provider should return a schema-valid continuation that advances or establishes a conversation situation, names authorized participants when supported, preserves the exact visible reply, and records only justified durable truths.
Registered D&D source paths prevent application-aware intent resolution

system.application-preview reports SCAN_PATH_NOT_FOUND for seven registered mechanics and procedure sources after the catalog moved to namespace directories. system.feature-search returns CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE and interaction planning returns RECIPE_RESOLVER_UNAVAILABLE, so the Inner AI cannot discover the contracts beneath intent.

All active dnd2024 source registrations should resolve the current namespace-directory catalog. Feature search and interaction planning should return automatically resolved effective application candidates without overlay identifiers.
Effects dry-run accepts a bundle the real commit rejects at the event-count guard

A 105-effect Shardwake world foundation passed commit(kind effects, dryRun true), but the identical commit failed with EVENT_COUNT_LIMIT. Splitting the same reviewed change into 61 and 44 effects succeeded.
Dry-run should evaluate the same event-count guard as commit, or should clearly report that commit-only guards remain and give the accepted maximum.
World-state synchronization excludes valid relationship-scoped world members

The Shardwake application state contains factions and knowledge records linked to the world root through their contract-defined in-world relationships. A later world-state sync rooted at world.shardwake rejects a new relationship to such a faction as WORLD_SCOPE_INVALID because only containment appears to establish scope.

The application world synchronizer should recognize the contract-defined in-world relationships used by factions, chronology, and knowledge, while still failing closed for genuinely cross-world records.
Automatic intent cannot route governed campaign creation

system.interaction-plan with plannerPreference automatic returned RECIPE_RESOLVER_UNAVAILABLE without searching or inspecting the active campaign procedure and mechanic contracts. Exact submitted proposals work.
The Inner AI should resolve campaign bootstrap intent from the active D&D campaign procedure and exact campaign mechanics, or return a contract-specific clarification.
Play continuity accepts unbound placeholder entity IDs and unverified transcript answers

In play-conversation.33881ad9b21e4f5588bebdd3f573831e the first structured truths used player as a subject entity ID while no bound play entities existed. A later request for verified scene affordances was answered from visible conversation continuity without a query.

Structured participant, location, and truth subject IDs must be copied only from trusted bound context or safe execution evidence. Requests for stored facts must delegate to a governed query and fail honestly when unavailable.
Strict namespace enforcement has no MCP namespace administration path

system.component-type.register correctly rejected dnd2024.game.core.campaign.current-scene because dnd2024.game.core.campaign was unregistered, but capabilities exposes no namespace query or registration commit. The machine had to use the catalog namespaces-only synchronization tool before MCP could continue.
A private operator should be able to inspect required namespace metadata and register or synchronize a reviewed namespace through the same governed capability surface used for component types.
Exact feature lookup does not reliably return an active mechanic

system.feature-search with id dnd2024.mechanic.campaign.create failed to return the exact active mechanic while system.catalog.record returned it. The exact web mechanic route consequently reported MECHANIC_UNKNOWN.
An exact qualified ID lookup should either return that active trusted record or an exact not-found result without lexical fallback; the web mechanic route should use the same exact inspection path.
Party intent cannot discover active application campaign actions

Resolving a bounded party-formation intent returned TRUSTED_FEATURE_NOT_FOUND with one search, zero inspections, and zero candidates. A direct effective catalog record read succeeded for dnd2024.mechanic.campaign.character.attach, but feature search for party creation returned no hits.
Intent discovery should return current effective campaign attachment and party-formation contracts so the planner can inspect and propose them.

Durable play context does not refresh trusted participants from the active campaign roster

The stored current situation still exposes only Tarin, so the no-forged-reference guard cannot admit the new exact campaign participants.
Before invoking the outer model, the host should enrich its allowed play references from the exact active campaign participation graph while preserving strict rejection of untrusted entity IDs.
D&D campaign location-visit action lacks an active application component mapping

Every effectComponentId declared by an active D&D campaign mechanic should resolve through the state-space application binding, including game.core.campaign.location-visit.
Inner planner cannot resolve active multi-chapter play actions

Intent-first requests for dice, clock advance, scene movement, affordances, visit recording, chapter advancement, and conversation continuation returned TRUSTED_FEATURE_NOT_FOUND, CONTRACT_NOT_INSPECTED, or RECIPE_RESOLVER_UNAVAILABLE even though active catalog contracts were exactly inspectable and verified caller-submitted proposals succeeded for most actions.

The Inner AI should discover the active application feature, inspect its exact contract, produce an inert proposal, and continue narration after confirmed execution without requiring qualified action IDs.
Registered campaign location-visit action still fails before committing

The campaign location-visit type was registered and the state space upgraded successfully. The campaign references Lantern Harbor and is linked to the active World and clock, but the exact verified location-visit proposal returned INTERACTION_EXECUTION_FAILED with MECHANIC_FAILED and committed no step.
The first visit should create the aggregate visit entity, component, and relationships atomically, or expose a safe contract-level reason.
commit(kind:"mechanic") non-dry-run writes fail with an opaque tool-level error, while dryRun:true on the identical payload validates cleanly.

Registered mechanic.game.core.world.location.register successfully via commit(kind:"mechanic") earlier in this session (operationId 8e31961a197f490cb71d78d6ad8d11f8). All subsequent non-dryRun commit(kind:"mechanic") calls fail with an unstructured 'An error occurred invoking commit' -- no error code, no why/fix. Confirmed across multiple different payloads, including mechanic.game.core.world.quest.register (validated clean on dryRun repeatedly, operationIds include 6280383b34a743b09306cf7f48b3a9cb and 5f51fb6dcb6744c7b5d692735bd3fa78) and a trivial 2-line test mechanic (mechanic.example.probe). Ruled out as causes: payload content/size, category choice (tried existing 'game.core.world.knowledge' and new 'game.core.world.quest'), near-duplicate match-phrase warning (non-blocking), missing procedure read (re-tried after reading procedure.mechanic.write, which then correctly appeared in proceduresYouDemonstrablyRead on the dry run -- still failed on real commit), and explicit status:'active' in payload. commit(kind:"effects") and commit(kind:"system.interaction-execute") continue to work normally throughout, so this appears isolated to the non-dryRun mechanic write path specifically.

commit(kind:"mechanic") without dryRun should either succeed (matching its clean dryRun validation) or return a structured error with a code and why/fix, consistent with every other commit kind in this system.
